doc.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 25, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Adapting to the future through social media
summary: He says the music will remain but delivery must adapt, pointing to Bria Skonberg, Benny Benack and Tony Glausi's social media.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young

blocks.x: that’s jazz and that’s, you know, but anyway Dick had that same vision of going to New York and making it and that was his first night. Certain people aren’t so lucky. I walked into New York and I had a Broadway show when I decided to permanently move there. Certainly I can talk to you about other things people can do and in fact in regard to what people should do now as opposed to before Covid or after, the music is still going to be there. It’s still going to be great music, but we have to adapt ourselves to the sort of new way of delivering it. Most people are already on that tract if you’re familiar with Bria Skonberg.

Benny Benack, there’s a guy named Tony Glausi, these are three trumpet players that are on it. Their social media presence is strong, they post almost every day or every other day with something. It’s informative and they’re great musicians and they’re good people. And I suggest to people to follow those kind of examples of what it’s going to feel like, be like and look like in the future.
